chunks: Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā al-ʿUbaydī narrated from al-Faḍl ibn al-Mubārak that he wrote to Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام.
Concerning a man who has a slave, and the slave became ill: is freeing him during his illness greater in reward for him, or should he leave him as a slave?

He said: If it is during an illness, then emancipation is better for him, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, frees with every limb of him a limb from the Fire. But if it is at the state of the presence of death, then leaving him as a slave is better for him than emancipating him.

key_terms.النَّارِ: the Fire, meaning punishment in the Hereafter
key_terms.الْعِتْقُ: emancipation or manumission of a slave
key_terms.حُضُورِ الْمَوْتِ: the onset or presence of death
key_terms.مَرَضِهِ: his illness; the state during which the ruling is being asked about

ai.seo_question: Is freeing a slave during illness better than doing so at the time of death?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about emancipating a slave when the slave falls ill versus when death is imminent. It indicates that emancipation during illness carries great reward, while emancipation at the point of death is less preferable, and it ties the act of freeing a slave to salvation from the Fire.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.3560 - Muhammad ibn Isa al-Ubaydi narrated from al-Fadl ibn al-Mubarak:
He wrote to Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad (as) asking about a man who owns a slave, and the slave becomes ill.
Is it better for the man to free him during his illness to gain a greater reward, or to leave him as a servant?

Imam (as) replied: "If it is during his illness, then freeing him is better for him because Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, frees a part of the master from the Fire for every part of the slave that is freed. However, if it is at the time of death, then leaving him as a servant is better than freeing him."
